global_lexicon.core_thesis: CatBoost predicts membrane fouling accurately with R2 = 0.8374 when engineers combine robust scaling, 5-day moving averages, and specific flux. Explainable AI shows that food-to-microorganism ratio and mixed liquor suspended solids control fouling progression.

key_terms.term: MBR (Membrane Bioreactor) [Bể phản ứng sinh học màng]
key_terms.definition: An advanced wastewater treatment system combining biological activated sludge treatment with membrane filtration.

key_terms.term: Membrane Fouling [Hiện tượng nghẹt màng (nhiễm bẩn màng)]
key_terms.definition: The unwanted accumulation of suspended solids, colloids, and biofilm on membrane surfaces or inside pores, decreasing filtration efficiency.

key_terms.term: TMP (Transmembrane Pressure) [Áp suất xuyên màng]
key_terms.definition: The pressure difference across a membrane that drives water through the filtration barrier (unit: kPa).

key_terms.term: Permeate Flux (Flux) [Lưu lượng dòng qua màng]
key_terms.definition: The volume of treated water passing through a unit membrane area per unit time (unit: L/(m2 h)).

key_terms.term: Specific Flux (Spec. Flux) [Tính thấm màng (Lưu lượng riêng)]
key_terms.definition: The ratio of permeate flux to TMP (Flux/TMP), representing the true hydraulic permeability of the membrane.

key_terms.term: F/M Ratio (Food-to-Microorganism Ratio) [Tỷ lệ thức ăn trên vi sinh vật]
key_terms.definition: The daily mass ratio of incoming organic substrate (COD) to microbial biomass (MLSS) in the reactor (unit: kgCOD/(kgMLSS d)).

key_terms.term: MLSS (Mixed Liquor Suspended Solids) [Chất rắn lơ lửng trong bùn hoạt tính]
key_terms.definition: The total concentration of suspended solids and biomass in the aeration tank (unit: mg/L).

key_terms.term: COD (Chemical Oxygen Demand) [Nhu cầu oxy hóa học]
key_terms.definition: The amount of oxygen required to chemically oxidize organic pollutants in wastewater (unit: mg/L).

key_terms.term: COD RM (COD Removal Efficiency) [Hiệu suất loại bỏ COD]
key_terms.definition: The percentage of chemical oxygen demand removed during biological oxidation and membrane filtration (unit: %).

key_terms.term: SV30 (Sludge Volume after 30 min) [Thể tích bùn lắng sau 30 phút]
key_terms.definition: The percentage of mixed liquor occupied by settled sludge after 30 minutes in a graduated cylinder (unit: %).

key_terms.term: SVI (Sludge Volume Index) [Chỉ số thể tích bùn]
key_terms.definition: The volume in milliliters occupied by one gram of MLSS after 30 minutes of settling, assessing sludge settleability (unit: mL/g).

key_terms.term: DO (Dissolved Oxygen) [Oxy hòa tan]
key_terms.definition: The concentration of dissolved molecular oxygen in the mixed liquor needed for aerobic respiration (unit: mg/L).

key_terms.term: Robust Scaling [Chuẩn hóa bền vững (Robust Scaling)]
key_terms.definition: A feature scaling technique that subtracts the median and divides by the interquartile range (IQR = Q3 - Q1), limiting outlier impact.

key_terms.term: Moving Average (MA) [Trung bình trượt (Moving Average)]
key_terms.definition: A rolling window transformation that smooths high-frequency noise and reflects historical delay in biological fouling processes.

key_terms.term: CatBoost (Categorical Boosting) [Thuật toán tăng cường CatBoost]
key_terms.definition: An open-source gradient boosting decision tree algorithm developed by Yandex that uses ordered boosting to prevent target leakage.

key_terms.term: XGBoost (eXtreme Gradient Boosting) [Thuật toán tăng cường XGBoost]
key_terms.definition: A scalable, distributed gradient boosting algorithm optimized for speed and predictive performance.

key_terms.term: XAI (Explainable Artificial Intelligence) [Trí tuệ nhân tạo có thể giải thích được]
key_terms.definition: Methods that give transparent, interpretable explanations for machine learning predictions.

key_terms.term: SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) [Giá trị giải thích phụ gia Shapley]
key_terms.definition: A game-theory technique that computes the fair marginal contribution of each feature to the model prediction.

key_terms.term: Permutation Importance [Độ quan trọng theo hoán vị]
key_terms.definition: A model inspection technique that measures the drop in prediction score after shuffling feature values.

key_terms.term: Shapiro-Wilk Test [Kiểm định phân phối chuẩn Shapiro-Wilk]
key_terms.definition: A statistical test that determines whether sample data follows a normal Gaussian distribution.

# Global Context Pack: Predictive Framework for Membrane Fouling in Full-Scale MBRs

## 1. Document Scope and Core Thesis
This study develops a machine learning framework to predict membrane fouling in full-scale membrane bioreactors (MBRs). The system treats real food processing wastewater over 194 operational days. CatBoost predicts membrane fouling accurately with R2 = 0.8374 when engineers combine robust scaling, 5-day moving averages, and specific flux. Explainable AI shows that food-to-microorganism ratio and mixed liquor suspended solids control fouling progression.

## 2. Experimental Setup and Four Test Cases
The plant operates submerged hollow fiber membrane modules with a daily average flowrate of 200 m3/d. The dataset tracks 194 daily measurements of operational parameters and biological indicators. The authors evaluate four distinct modeling cases:
- Case I: Basic parameters predict Transmembrane Pressure (TMP).
- Case II: Basic parameters plus COD removal efficiency predict TMP.
- Case III: Basic parameters predict Specific Flux.
- Case IV: Basic parameters plus COD removal efficiency predict Specific Flux.
Specific flux directly quantifies membrane permeability and serves as the primary target parameter.

## 3. Preprocessing and Feature Engineering Methods
The Shapiro-Wilk test confirms that 9 of 10 process features deviate from normal distributions. Robust scaling normalizes variables using the median and interquartile range (IQR = Q3 - Q1). This transformation removes the distorting influence of extreme operational outliers. A 5-day moving average smooths high-frequency sensor noise. This moving average also accounts for biological retention delays and cumulative fouling formation.

## 4. Model Architectures and Performance Benchmarks
The study compares four linear statistical models against two gradient boosting tree models:
- Statistical: Linear Regression, Ridge Regression, Lasso Regression, and Elastic Net.
- Machine Learning: XGBoost and CatBoost.
On raw data, linear models perform poorly (R2 < 0.20), while CatBoost achieves R2 = 0.7317. Applying robust scaling and a 5-day moving average elevates CatBoost accuracy to R2 = 0.8374 and reduces error by 27.8 percent. CatBoost outperforms XGBoost (R2 = 0.7186) across all test cases.

## 5. Explainable AI (XAI) Findings
The authors apply three interpretation methods: Built-in Importance, Permutation Importance, and SHAP. All three methods identify the 5-day moving average of F/M ratio (F/M_MA5) as the most critical feature (SHAP = 26.17 percent). Mixed liquor suspended solids (MLSS) ranks second (SHAP = 10.04 percent). SHAP summary plots show that elevated F/M ratios and high MLSS accelerate cake layer accumulation. Lower pH values also increase fouling risk by altering sludge flocs and biofilm dynamics. Plant operators can adjust organic loading and sludge wasting rates to prevent membrane clogging proactively.

## 6. Structure of the Document
- Section 1: Introduction, fouling mechanisms, research gaps, and study goals.
- Section 2: Materials and Methods, pilot data collection, EDA protocols, scaling formulas, model equations, and XAI theory.
- Section 3: Results, distribution statistics, correlation matrices, model benchmarks, prediction curves, and SHAP interpretations.
- Section 4: Conclusions, plant integration recommendations, study limitations, and future research paths.
